signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Disadvantage
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard establishes JPY as the weekly leader at +0.721% across 7 pairs, while AUD is the clear laggard at -0.741% across 4 pairs. This generates a 1.462% leader-to-laggard bilateral spread, triggering an alert under the theme threshold. AUD/JPY trades at 107.504, compressed by risk aversion as VIX sits at 25.5 (elevated volatility) following equity declines and Middle East geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. JPY outperforms despite a steep carry disadvantage against AUD, where RBA at 4.85% vs BoJ at 1.25% maintains a 360bp nominal spread and an AONIA vs TONA basis of 362bp favoring AUD. Retail sentiment sits at 88% long, compounding unwind vulnerability as risk-off flows dominate structural yield incentives. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; safe-haven demand overrides substantial carry buffer. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change and Wage Price Index at 00:30 UTC. Risk: VIX drops back below 20.0 and employment beats sharply, reviving high-beta carry demand.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Fed Hawkish Hold
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.49, holding above its SMA20 at 158.33 and SMA50 at 157.63. While the 270bp SOFR vs TONA carry spread keeps the baseline supported alongside Fed Chair remarks warning that inflation is not moving in the right direction, 160.00 remains the critical psychological threshold that previously invited official intervention scrutiny. The options market is heavily positioned for a sharp downside event, evidenced by a 25-delta Risk Reversal at -1.71 alongside 1M ATM implied volatility of 7.1% against 5.3% 30-day realized volatility, generating a notable +1.7% volatility risk premium. With leveraged funds holding net short -23,913 contracts (90th percentile of its 52-week range), the pair faces asymmetric unwind risk if spot tests 160.00. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; structural carry advantage offset by extreme options put skew. Catalyst: Japan National Core CPI at 23:30 UTC. Risk: A sustained breakout above 160.00 without official resistance compresses risk reversals back toward zero.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Positioning + Rates Drag
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0997, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1152, SMA50 at 1.1272, and SMA200 at 1.1518 in an established technical downtrend. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds holding net short -98,604 contracts, sitting in the 6th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.58, indicating stretched institutional positioning. Meanwhile, the Fed 4.00% (on hold) vs ECB 2.65% (on hold) policy rate gap provides a 135bp carry advantage to the dollar, reflected in a +149bp SOFR vs €STR spread. Intraday real-yield dynamics continue to favor USD, with US 5Y yields adding +39bp over 5 sessions, led by a +35bp rise in real yields to 2.68%. Stretched short positioning warns of exhaustion, but structural monetary divergence keeps upside strictly capped. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent policy divergence dominates oversold positioning. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI YoY print at 10:00 UTC. Risk: A sharp upside surprise in Eurozone core inflation triggers an aggressive short-squeeze toward the 1.1152 SMA20.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Sentiment Divergence + Technical Extension
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4299, maintaining a clear technical uptrend above its SMA20 at 1.4092 and SMA50 at 1.4101, extended 3.11 ATR above its 20-day moving average. Retail positioning on Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 92% short bias, directly contradicting institutional leveraged funds, which scaled back short exposure with a +15,077 contract weekly shift to sit at 42nd percentile neutrality. The Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.50% differential delivers a 150bp policy spread and a +138bp SOFR vs CORRA basis that structurally penalizes short holders. The BEER valuation model registers USD/CAD as rich at +1.76σ, yet one-sided retail fading against dominant carry continues to fuel short-covering momentum. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; contrarian squeeze dynamics against retail short crowding. Catalyst: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle speech at 22:24 UTC. Risk: Daily close below 1.4092 SMA20 validates mean-reversion toward fair value.
